elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer commits to purchase “no minimum amount,” and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer owes fees only for Services it orders or uses.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly provides that Customer “pays only for Services ordered or used.”

elements.element: Any minimum purchase commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause demonstrably imposes no minimum purchase commitment, so there is no commitment extending beyond the current 12-month term. The retained reference to the next three years does not impose a minimum.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any such commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause demonstrably imposes no commitment to reduce; therefore, the condition requiring a 30-day reduction right does not arise.

elements.element: Any shortfall against such a commitment is resolved by a true-up.
elements.evidence: Because there is no minimum commitment, there can be no shortfall requiring a true-up.

elements.element: No penalty applies for a shortfall against such a commitment.
elements.evidence: The take-or-pay obligation and associated no-reduction language were removed, and no minimum commitment remains against which a shortfall penalty could apply.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position by eliminating any minimum and limiting payment to ordered or used Services. The fallback protections are also satisfied because their triggering condition—a minimum commitment—is demonstrably absent. The revision is limited to the minimum-commitment provision and is consistent with Section 12.3. Drafting quality is reduced because “commits to purchase no minimum amount in each of the next three years” is awkward and unnecessarily retains a three-year reference, although its operative meaning is adequately clear.
